XVII.}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=17|verse=1}}}}ND vvhen they had vvalked through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, vvhere there vvas a synagogue of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=2}}† And Paul according to his custome entred in vnto them, & three Sabboths he discoursed to them out of the Scriptures, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=3}}† declaring and insinuating that it behoued {{sc|Christ}} to suffer and to rise againe from the dead: and that this is {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}, vvhom I preach to you. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=4}}† And certaine of them beleeued, and vvere ioyned to Paul and Silas, and of the Gentiles that serued God a great multitude, and noble vvomen not a fevv. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=5}}† But the Ievves {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Zelantes''. This is the zeale of Heretikes, and a liuely paterne of their dealing at this day against Catholike Priests and preachers and the good ''Iasons'' that receiue them.}}∷ enuying, & taking vnto them of the rascal sort certaine naughtie men, and making a tumult, stirred the citie: and besetting Iasons house, sought to bring them forth vnto the people. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=6}}† And not finding them, they drevv Iason and certaine brethren to the princes of the citie, crying, That these are they that stirre vp the vvorld, and are come hither, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=7}}† vvhom Iason hath receiued, and al these doe against the decrees of Cæsar, saying that there is an other king, {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=8}}† And they moued the people, and the princes of the citie hearing these things. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=9}}† And taking a satisfaction of Iason and of the rest, they dimissed them. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=10}}† But the brethren forthwith by night sent away Paul and Silas vnto Berœa.

Vvho vvhen they vvere come, entred into the synagogue of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=11}}† (And these were more noble then they that are at Thessalonica, vvho receiued the vvord vvith al greedines, daily {{sup|‖}} searching the scriptures, if these things vvere so. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=12}}† And many surely of them beleeued, and of honest women Gentiles, and men not a few.) {{verse|chapter=17|verse=13}}† And vvhen the Iewes in Thessalonica vnderstood, that at Berœa also the vvord of God was preached by Paul, they came thither also, mouing and troubling the multitude. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=14}}† And then immediatly the<noinclude>{{rh|||brethren}}</noinclude>
